section_title: What makes someone useful to the Master?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 20 A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use. 21 So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.

22 Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart. 23 But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling. 24 And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing. 25 He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth. 26 Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.

context_lines: Paul pictures a large household with different vessels for different purposes. He urges cleansing from what is unfit so that a person can be set apart, useful to the Master and ready for good work.

The instructions that follow show what that readiness looks like: turning from youthful passions and pursuing righteousness, faith, love and peace alongside others who call on the Lord sincerely. It includes refusing foolish disputes without becoming a quarrelsome person.

Timothy must still teach and correct. He is to do so with kindness, patience and gentleness, hoping that God will grant repentance and release people from the devil’s trap. The aim of correction is their recovery into the truth.
common_interpretation_lines: [Calvin](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/2_timothy/2.htm) and [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-second-epistle-to-timothy/) both connect the vessels with the church and the call to separate from wickedness. Calvin recognizes a mixture of good and bad people in the visible community; Wesley notes that a vessel intended for honorable use may be put to a bad use. The picture calls hearers to a life fit for God’s service.

Both read the final instructions as requiring patient, gentle teaching and dependence on God for repentance. Refusing a quarrel does not mean abandoning every person who disagrees. Calvin particularly stresses continuing to seek the recovery of people who now appear resistant, because God can change them.
god_plan_lines: [Ephesians 2:8–10](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/2.htm) joins salvation by grace with being made in Christ for good works. That gives the wider setting for becoming useful to the Master: a life shaped by grace and prepared for service.

[Galatians 6:1–2](https://biblehub.com/bsb/galatians/6.htm) calls for gently restoring someone caught in wrongdoing and bearing one another’s burdens. Timothy’s correction shares that purpose of recovery and care within God’s people, rather than winning a contest at someone else’s expense.
